title: A work order for an internal customer is created internal
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer, with one asset, asset 1.
  • Use a desktop browser at least 1440 pixels wide.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Work Order.
  2. Pick customer A.
  3. Pick asset 1.
  4. Click Save in the New Work Order window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • The "Internal" badge shows next to customer A.
  • There is no "No Charge" checkbox and no category select in the window.

Step 3:

  • Asset 1 is picked.

Step 4:

  • The new work order opens with one "Internal" badge next to its status.
  • It offers "Close Work Order" where a billable work order offers "Create invoice".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R1: “In the New Work Order dialog, picking a customer with the Internal customer flag shows the "Internal" badge next to the customer name with an info icon; the tooltip reads "Internal customer: no prices, no invoice. Posts to [category], from the asset." or "... from the customer." (the latter also when neither the asset nor the customer has a category of its own and the default Internal category applies). There is no checkbox to tick and no category to pick on the work order. The work order is created internal with the category resolved as: the asset's Internal category (S1-R15), else the customer's default (S1-R7), else the default Internal category; it is re-resolved while the work order is open when the asset changes or when the category of the asset or the customer is edited (a closed work order never changes), archived categories are skipped (S1-R16), and it can be changed on the asset or the customer, never on the work order. A work order created from an inspection, or from a maintenance reminder once Maintenance Reminders ship, follows the same rule: it is internal when its customer carries the flag at creation, and otherwise billable.”
  • S2-N3: “If the selected customer is an internal customer, the "No Charge" checkbox is not shown in the New Work Order dialog and a billable work order of that customer offers no Convert action (S2-R2, S2-R7). An open no-charge work order on a customer that was flagged afterwards (S1-R11) keeps Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6).”
  • Key Decisions: “Internal is a flag on the customer, not on the work order, not a work order type and not a new status.”
  • Terminology: “Internal work order → a work order whose customer carried the Internal customer flag when the work order was created or last changed customer. Not a work order type and not a status.”
  • Feature Overview: “Internal work orders come from internal customers. The shop flags its own company (and any sister company) as an internal customer once: in the modal that opens the first time the Internal Work Orders setting is switched on (nobody is preselected: the location is not necessarily a customer and the names differ), or later with the Internal customer checkbox at the bottom of Edit Customer. Settings > Work Orders holds the toggle, that one-time modal and two hints: a link to the categories page and a link to the QuickBooks mapping. Every internal customer carries a default internal category, General Internal unless changed on Edit Customer; an asset of an internal customer can carry its own category (Edit Asset). A new internal work order takes the asset's category, else the customer's, else General Internal. Nobody picks a category or an account on the work order; the Internal badge and its tooltip say where it posts.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
